harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed the supplied handler on node1:9097 using RHEL 10’s native `systemd-socket-activate --accept --inetd` compatibility mode. Sequential and concurrent clients pass, each connection receives a separate non-root handler process, no handlers remain afterward, and operation persisted through one-at-a-time restarts of both nodes.
actions_performed: Used a dynamic non-root identity and systemd service hardening.
Restricted firewalld access on port 9097 to node2 only, persistently.
Verified PING→PONG and all other tested lines→ERROR from node2.
Verified 12 sequential clients and eight concurrent clients.
Preserved protocol files and their permissions/content hashes on both nodes.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually, proving changed boot identities and full recovery.
Removed temporary test artifacts and confirmed zero remaining handler processes or connections.

evidence.summary: RHEL repositories provide no inetd/xinetd package; the installed OS-native activator explicitly supports inetd stdin/stdout protocol and one-child-per-connection mode.
Validated unit is enabled and active, uses DynamicUser, listens on TCP 9097, and firewalld permits only node2’s address.

evidence.requirement: PING returns PONG; other lines return ERROR; sequential clients complete
evidence.summary: Both protocol branches passed and 12/12 sequential connections completed successfully.

evidence.requirement: Separate handler per concurrent connection and no leaked processes
evidence.summary: Eight concurrent connections produced eight distinct non-root handler children; all returned correctly, exited code 0, and final child/connection counts were zero.

evidence.requirement: Protocol notes and supplied handler preserved; OS and kernel unchanged
evidence.summary: Pre/post SHA-256 hashes match on both nodes; both remain RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64.

Healthy baseline captured, safe reboot acknowledged, boot ID changed from 19062a82-6390-435d-a09f-4dba1593d529 to af72988a-919d-418c-993b-fb2f158fd253, and service/data/security plus node2 client behavior recovered.

Healthy baseline captured, safe reboot acknowledged, boot ID changed from 4ebdfa06-919e-48a9-8a15-475d9007662c to b103045b-591a-42ff-91e9-f9d416ad9e95, and node health/data/network plus the node2→node1 protocol recovered.
Service is enabled and active after both restarts, final client behavior passes, SELinux/firewalld remain active, no failed units or test artifacts remain, and no handler processes are left behind.
